input.reasoning_summary:
After reviewing the weaknesses, my initial CONTRADICTED verdict stands.

W1 (offsetting effects interpretation): This is refuted. The claim explicitly states Latin America "drove" unit case volume "growth." With worldwide growth at 0% and Latin America also at 0%, Latin America contributed nothing to growth - neither positive nor negative. The only segment with positive growth was EMEA at 3%. A segment that is flat (0%) cannot be described as the primary driver of growth.

W2 (table formatting ambiguity): This is refuted. E6's table clearly shows two columns: "Unit Cases" and "Concentrate Sales." The dash (—) symbol represents 0% for Latin America's unit cases, and (1) represents -1% for concentrate sales. This is confirmed by E3 from the same 10-K which states "In Latin America, unit case volume was even" - explicitly confirming 0% growth. The quarterly data showing -1% or -2% in some quarters is consistent with a full-year result of 0% (even).

W3 (absolute volume interpretation): This is refuted. E6 shows percentage changes, and with 0% growth, Latin America contributed zero additional unit cases in absolute terms as well. There is no way to interpret 0% growth as "driving" growth, whether in percentage or absolute terms.

The claim is contradicted because Latin America had 0% unit case volume growth in 2025 and therefore could not have been the primary driver of growth. EMEA was the only segment with positive growth at 3%.
